audit.whatIsWrong: Ornn's slots are mixed up through the content layer. The early prose calls it 'his E Bellows Breath' and says 'the knockup cuts your Q animation... the instant he channels'; wants.you[1] repeats 'his E Bellows Breath knockup'; wants.foe[0] invents 'his passive Bellows Breath and W Frailty resistances'; whys[2] and the mid prose describe an 'E-W knockup chain'.
audit.why: Bellows Breath is W, not E, and it has no knockup at all - Riot's text says enemies hit by the final gout of flame become Brittle. The knockup is Searing Charge (E), and it only happens on terrain collision: 'If Ornn collides with terrain while charging, the impact creates a shockwave around him which deals damage and knocks up enemies.' The passive is Living Forge, which grants bonus Armor and Magic Resist from all sources and lets him forge items anywhere - it has nothing to do with either ability the page attached to it.
audit.corrected: All five abilities named correctly, with Bellows Breath as the Brittle applier and Searing Charge as the terrain-collision knockup.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page says 'stand near walls for his Q' but never says the decisive thing: Volcanic Rupture builds him a wall wherever he wants one.
audit.why: Riot's text for Volcanic Rupture: 'After a small delay, a magma pillar forms at the end location.' That pillar is terrain, and Searing Charge knocks up on terrain collision - so Ornn does not need to corner you against the map. He drops a pillar and charges into it. Advice that only says 'avoid walls' leaves the player safe in open lane and still knocked up.
audit.corrected: The pillar-into-charge setup written into whys[2], the early prose, the mid prose, wants.you[1] and wants.foe[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: Call of the Forge God is called a 'double-knockup' in whys[4] and the Level 6 spike, and carries no cooldown or range.
audit.why: Riot's text: the elemental travels toward him, and enemies run over take damage, are slowed and are made Brittle - no knockup on that pass. The knockup comes from the recast, when Ornn charges into the elemental and redirects it. It is 140/120/100s at 2500 range. Calling it a double-knockup makes the first pass sound lethal and the recast sound routine, which is backwards: the first pass is the setup and the recast is the thing that ends your combo.
audit.corrected: Both fields rewritten with the two-stage description and the 140s rank-1 cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read Riven, Skill, Ornn, Ornn, Riven, Ornn, Ornn while the packet chart reads Skill, Riven, Ornn, Ornn, Ornn, Ornn, Ornn.
audit.why: The page's own whys already say so: whys[0] states neither side has a kill pattern at Level 1 and 'both sides farm' (Skill), whys[1] calls Level 2 'your only clean all-in window' (Riven), and whys[4] says 'never hard-engage an Ornn with R ready' (Ornn). Level 1 and Level 2 were simply swapped, and Level 6 was given to Riven by the boilerplate Blade-of-the-Exile why despite the content why saying the opposite. The ornn__riven mirror flipped exactly these three rows.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1 and 4 flipped as one atomic paired group in both layers to Skill, Riven, Ornn, Ornn, Ornn, Ornn, Ornn, with ratings moved to match.

edits.before: W comes online and Ornn cannot match your burst burst before his passive resistances fully stack — your only clean all-in window.
edits.after: Ki Burst comes online and Living Forge has almost no resistances stacked yet — this is your one clean all-in window in the whole lane.

edits.before: His E-W knockup chain interrupts your Q animation and flips trades; Ornn's passive tankiness makes prolonged fights favour him.
edits.after: Volcanic Rupture's pillar gives him a wall to Searing Charge into, and that knockup cuts Broken Wings dead — long fights belong to him.

edits.before: His R double-knockup deletes your commit entirely and his enhanced stats are fully online — never hard-engage an Ornn with R ready.
edits.after: Call of the Forge God slows and Brittles on the first pass and knocks up on his recast — 140s at rank 1, so never engage an Ornn holding it.

edits.before: Ornn's R double-knockup hard-interrupts your Q-chain and kills you outright if you are even slightly behind — respect it completely.
edits.after: Call of the Forge God's elemental Brittles and slows you, then his recast charge knocks you up — that second pass is what ends your combo.

edits.before: At Level 1 you are both even — Ornn has no real kill threat and neither do you without W. The moment Level 2 hits, E onto him, burn W stun, and run the full Q-chain before his passive resistance procs give him effective stats. His E Bellows Breath is the trade-ender: the knockup cuts your Q animation and lets him walk back to tower, so time your own E dash to dodge it the instant he channels. If you hit a clean Level 2 all-in and he blows Flash or takes heavy HP loss, he is forced to back or farm at a disadvantage. If he absorbs the combo and walks back healthy, respect his passive tankiness and do not greed for a second trade — you burn more resources than he does.
edits.after: At Level 1 you are both even — Ornn has no kill threat and neither do you without Ki Burst. The moment Level 2 hits, Valor onto him, burn the stun, and run the full Broken Wings chain before Living Forge's resistances amount to anything. Searing Charge (E) is the trade-ender, but only near terrain: he charges 450 units and the knockup fires on wall collision, including the magma pillar Volcanic Rupture leaves behind, so he can build his own wall. Fight in open lane away from that pillar and sidestep the charge line. If a clean Level 2 all-in takes his Flash or half his HP he is stuck backing. If he absorbs it and walks off healthy, do not greed a second trade.

edits.before: Levels 4 through 5 are where this lane starts to tilt against you. Ornn has enough stacked HP and his E-W chain is consistent now, so a full engage from you into a well-timed E knocks you airborne mid-combo and the trade swings back in his favour. Farm and harass with the tip of Q, but do not hard commit without your E shield active and a clean W angle. Level 6 flips the lane decisively: his R is a long-range double-knockup that covers his retreat or turns a chase into your death. Never fight into an Ornn who has R available at even HP — look to shove, roam mid, and convert your early lead into another lane rather than fighting a tank who now one-shots your commit.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 5 are where this lane starts to tilt against you. Ornn has stacked HP, and Volcanic Rupture's pillar plus Searing Charge is a knockup he sets up himself: pillar down, charge into it, and your combo ends mid-animation. Bellows Breath is the other half — it makes you Brittle, which is what turns his chip into real damage. Harass with the tip of Broken Wings, but never commit without Valor held and a clean stun angle. Level 6 flips the lane decisively: Call of the Forge God reaches 2500 units, slowing and Brittling on the first pass and knocking up on the recast. Never fight an Ornn at even HP with it up — shove, roam, and cash the lead elsewhere.

edits.before: Late game Ornn with Masterwork upgrades for his entire team becomes effectively unkillable in a straight 1v1 and a teamfight menace with two knockups. Your window to close the game was Levels 2-4; if the game drags past 25 minutes, itemised Ornn absorbs your full combo, E-W chains you, and his team capitalises while you are grounded. Focus on splitting and pressuring side lanes to force him away from his team rather than looking to duel — Wind Slash will not execute a champion with 5000+ HP unless he is already below 30%, and he will rarely reach that threshold against a coordinated team.
edits.after: Late game Ornn with Masterwork upgrades for his entire team becomes effectively unkillable in a straight 1v1 and a teamfight menace with two separate knockups. Your window to close the game was Levels 2-4; if the game drags past 25 minutes, itemised Ornn absorbs your full combo, pillars you into a Searing Charge knockup, and his team collects while you are airborne. Split and pressure side lanes to drag him away from his team rather than duelling him — Wind Slash will not execute a champion with 5000+ HP unless he is already very low, and against a coordinated team he rarely gets there.

edits.before: Dodge his E Bellows Breath knockup with your own E dash to deny his trade pattern
edits.after: Dodge Searing Charge (E) with Valor and stay off his magma pillar to deny the knockup

edits.before: Farm safely behind his passive Bellows Breath and W Frailty resistances until he is tanky enough to ignore your combo
edits.after: Farm safely behind Living Forge's compounding resistances until he is tanky enough to ignore your whole combo

edits.before: Land his E-W knockup sequence to interrupt your Q-chain and flip the trade
edits.after: Drop a pillar and Searing Charge into it to knock you out of Broken Wings

notes: PACKET DEFECT: the brief's top-level games is 1489 while packet.games is 1470. The ornn__riven mirror recorded the same class of mismatch on Olaf; someone should decide which figure the pages cite. The slot confusion here was severe - Bellows Breath was called an E, a passive and a knockup in three different fields, and 'W Frailty' is not an Ornn ability at all. The highest-value new fact is that Volcanic Rupture's magma pillar is terrain, so Searing Charge's knockup does not require a map wall: 'avoid walls' was safe-sounding advice that does not actually keep the player safe. Chart rows 0, 1 and 4 proposed as one atomic paired group matching the packet and the ornn__riven mirror.
